title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom (poem: A Tiger in the Zoo)

learn.hook: Imagine being told which bench, bus or school you may use because of the colour of your skin. That was life under apartheid.
points: 'Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom' is from Mandela's autobiography; it describes his swearing-in as South Africa's first Black President on 10 May 1994.
Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial separation and discrimination; the word means 'apartness'.
Mandela spent 27 years in prison before his release in 1990; for him, freedom meant freeing both the oppressed and the oppressor.
Simple past for a finished action at a stated time: 'He became President in 1994.'

Present perfect for a past action linked to now, often with since/for/already: 'South Africa has changed since 1994.' Past perfect for the earlier of two past actions: 'He had spent 27 years in prison before he was freed.'

example.q: Fill in: 'By 1994, apartheid ___ (end), and Mandela ___ (become) President.'
steps: Two past actions: apartheid ending came first, then Mandela became President.
The earlier action takes the past perfect: had ended.
The later action, at a known past time, takes the simple past: became.
example.answer: By 1994, apartheid had ended, and Mandela became President.

learn.reallife: India too fought for freedom and wrote equality into its Constitution. Mandela admired Mahatma Gandhi, who began his struggle against racial injustice in South Africa.

items.text: Mandela ___ President of South Africa in 1994.
The guests ___ before the ceremony began.
Every year, people ___ Freedom Day in South Africa on 27 April.
I ___ already read the chapter, so I can answer now.

options: A system of racial separation and discrimination in South Africa
A South African festival of freedom
A kind of election in South Africa
quiz.explain: Apartheid kept people apart and treated them unequally by race.
steps: 'Apartheid' means 'apartness' in Afrikaans.
It was a system of racial separation and discrimination in South Africa.
Answer: A system of racial separation and discrimination in South Africa
quiz.mistake: Thinks it was something positive because the lesson ends in freedom

quiz.q: On which date was Nelson Mandela sworn in as President of South Africa?
quiz.explain: The inauguration took place on 10 May 1994; 1990 is the year he was released from prison.
steps: Mandela was released from prison in 1990.
He was sworn in as President on 10 May 1994.
Answer: 10 May 1994
quiz.mistake: Confuses his release in 1990 with his inauguration

quiz.q: Passage: 'Freedom,' said Dadaji, 'is not only breaking your own chains. It is also making sure nobody else stays chained.' He spent his life teaching village children to read. According to Dadaji, what else does freedom mean?
options: Making sure nobody else stays chained
quiz.explain: He says freedom is also making sure nobody else stays chained.
steps: Dadaji says freedom is not only breaking your own chains.
It is also making sure nobody else stays chained.
Answer: Making sure nobody else stays chained
quiz.mistake: Stops reading after the first half of the sentence

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: 'Mandela ___ President in 1994.'
quiz.explain: 'In 1994' is a finished past time, so simple past is used.
steps: 'In 1994' is a finished past time.
A finished past time takes the simple past: became.
Answer: became
quiz.mistake: Uses present perfect with a fixed past time

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: 'South Africa ___ a lot since apartheid ended.'
quiz.explain: 'Since' links the past to now, so present perfect is used.
steps: 'Since apartheid ended' links the past to now.
That needs the present perfect: has changed.
Answer: has changed

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: 'By the time he was freed, Mandela ___ 27 years in prison.'
quiz.explain: The prison years came before he was freed, so the earlier past action takes the past perfect.
steps: The 27 years in prison happened before he was freed — the earlier of two past actions.
The earlier action takes the past perfect: had spent.
Answer: had spent
quiz.mistake: Does not see that two past actions need past perfect for the earlier one

quiz.q: What is the noun form of 'oppress'?
quiz.explain: -ion makes the noun; -ive makes an adjective; -ly makes an adverb; 'oppressful' is not a word.
steps: The suffix -ion makes a noun (oppress → oppression).
-ive makes an adjective and -ly an adverb; 'oppressful' is not a word.
Answer: Oppression
quiz.mistake: Mixes up suffixes for nouns and adjectives

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'freedom'?
quiz.explain: Bondage means being bound or enslaved; the others mean freedom.
steps: Liberty, independence and release all mean freedom.
The opposite is bondage — being bound or enslaved.
Answer: Bondage
quiz.mistake: Picks a synonym instead of an antonym

teach.ask: Gappu: What was apartheid, and why do we say 'Mandela became President in 1994', not 'has become'?
teach.praise: Chirrup! Apartheid separated people by race, and a finished time like 1994 needs the simple past. Got it!
teach.nudge: Was apartheid about separating people? And which tense goes with a fixed past time?

revise.summary: Mandela's autobiography describes his swearing-in as South Africa's first Black President on 10 May 1994, after apartheid. We also practise simple past, present perfect and past perfect.
focus: Recall key facts: apartheid, 27 years in prison, release in 1990, swearing-in on 10 May 1994.
Explain what freedom meant for Mandela: freeing both the oppressed and the oppressor.
Choose simple past, present perfect or past perfect from time signals.
remember: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial separation and discrimination; the word means 'apartness'.
Simple past for a finished action at a stated time: 'He became President in 1994.'
Present perfect for a past action linked to now (since/for/already); past perfect for the earlier of two past actions.
traps: Don't confuse his release in 1990 with his inauguration on 10 May 1994.
Don't use present perfect with a fixed past time like 'in 1994'.
Don't miss that the earlier of two past actions needs the past perfect: 'had spent'.

learn.hook: A tiger that should rule a jungle paces a few steps of concrete, up and down. Can a poem make us feel its anger?
points: 'A Tiger in the Zoo' by Leslie Norris contrasts a tiger's angry, helpless life in a cage with the free life it should have in the forest.
Contrast places two opposite ideas side by side (cage vs jungle) to make both sharper.
Imagery is language that creates pictures, sounds or feelings in the reader's mind.
Alliteration repeats the same first consonant sound in nearby words: 'guava groves'.
Enjambment is when a sentence runs on into the next line without a pause.

example.q: Poem: The parakeet in the iron cage / Repeats the words we say; / But in his dreams the guava groves / Of Nashik call him away. Which device is in 'guava groves', and what contrast does the poem make?
steps: 'guava groves' repeats the 'g' sound at the start of words, which is alliteration.
The bird is in an 'iron cage' but dreams of open guava groves.
So the poem sets captivity against freedom.
example.answer: Alliteration; the contrast is between the cage (captivity) and the guava groves (freedom).

learn.reallife: Wildlife reserves like Jim Corbett and Kaziranga try to protect animals in their natural homes so they can live freely.

games.title: Devices and the poem
items: 'A Tiger in the Zoo' was written by Leslie Norris.
Leslie Norris is the poet.
In 'A Tiger in the Zoo', the tiger is shown content in its cage.
The tiger is angry and helpless; it belongs in the wild.
'Sunil sells samosas' is an example of alliteration.
The 's' sound repeats at the start of words.
Imagery appeals only to the sense of sight.
Imagery can appeal to any sense: sight, sound, smell, touch or taste.
Enjambment means a sentence continues into the next line without a pause.
The thought runs on past the line break.
Contrast places two similar ideas side by side.
Contrast places opposite ideas side by side.

quiz.q: Who wrote 'A Tiger in the Zoo'?
steps: 'A Tiger in the Zoo' is in this chapter.
It was written by Leslie Norris.
Answer: Leslie Norris
quiz.mistake: Mixes up poets of the same book

quiz.q: What is the main contrast in 'A Tiger in the Zoo'?
options: Summer and winter in the zoo
The tiger's life in a cage and its life in the wild
Day and night in a village
quiz.explain: The poem sets the cage against the free forest life the tiger should have.
steps: The poem describes the tiger in its cage and imagines its life in the forest.
So the main contrast is cage life versus wild life.
Answer: The tiger's life in a cage and its life in the wild
quiz.mistake: Reads the poem as just a description of a zoo

quiz.q: Poem: The parakeet in the iron cage / Repeats the words we say; / But in his dreams the guava groves / Of Nashik call him away. Which device is used in 'guava groves'?
quiz.explain: The 'g' sound repeats at the start of both words.
steps: Alliteration repeats the same starting sound in nearby words.
'guava groves' repeats the 'g' sound.
Answer: Alliteration

quiz.q: Poem: The parakeet in the iron cage / Repeats the words we say; / But in his dreams the guava groves / Of Nashik call him away. What does the parakeet dream of?
quiz.explain: Lines 3-4 say the guava groves of Nashik call him in his dreams.
steps: Lines 3–4 say what calls him in his dreams.
It is the guava groves of Nashik.
Answer: The guava groves of Nashik
quiz.mistake: Picks what the bird does in the cage, not what he dreams

options: Language that creates pictures or feelings in the reader's mind
A sentence running into the next line
Saying the opposite of what you mean
quiz.explain: Imagery appeals to the senses so we can picture a scene.
steps: Imagery appeals to the senses.
It is language that creates pictures or feelings in the reader's mind.
Answer: Language that creates pictures or feelings in the reader's mind
quiz.mistake: Mixes up imagery with other devices

options: A sentence running on into the next line without a pause
A repeated line at the end of every stanza
quiz.explain: In enjambment the thought continues past the end of the line.
steps: Enjambment means the sentence does not stop at the end of a line.
It runs on into the next line without a pause.
Answer: A sentence running on into the next line without a pause
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with rhyme or refrain

options: Kept locked up and not free
quiz.explain: A captive animal is confined and not free.
steps: A captive animal is confined.
So captive means kept locked up and not free.
Answer: Kept locked up and not free
quiz.mistake: Links the word to 'capture the moment' (a photo) instead of confinement

quiz.q: Which line best shows a contrast between captivity and freedom?
options: 'He paces up and down all day.'
'Behind bars he paces; in the jungle he would roam.'
quiz.explain: It sets 'behind bars' against 'roam in the jungle', two opposite states.
steps: A contrast needs two opposite states in one line.
'Behind bars he paces; in the jungle he would roam' sets captivity against freedom.
Answer: 'Behind bars he paces; in the jungle he would roam.'
quiz.mistake: Picks a line that shows only one side

teach.ask: Gappu: Why does the poet show the tiger in the cage AND in the forest? What is that trick called?
teach.praise: Roar-chirp! Showing cage and jungle side by side is contrast. Now I feel how much the tiger misses the forest!
teach.nudge: What two places or states does the poem set against each other?

revise.summary: 'A Tiger in the Zoo' by Leslie Norris contrasts a tiger's angry, helpless life in a cage with the free life it should have in the forest. We also learn contrast, imagery, alliteration and enjambment.
focus: Explain the main contrast: life in the cage vs life in the wild.
Spot alliteration, imagery and enjambment in lines.
Pick lines that show both sides of a contrast.
remember: Contrast places two opposite ideas side by side (cage vs jungle) to make both sharper.
Imagery is language that creates pictures, sounds or feelings in the reader's mind.
Alliteration repeats the same first consonant sound in nearby words: 'guava groves'.
Enjambment is when a sentence runs on into the next line without a pause.
traps: Don't read the poem as just a description of a zoo; it is about captivity vs freedom.
Don't confuse sound repetition (alliteration) with comparison.
A contrast line must show both sides, not only one.
